_comment: Pilot (500-species) experiment queue. Runs sequentially on one GPU via run_experiments.py. Baseline reference: runs/pilot500_vitb = lr 1e-4, no warmup, no grad-clip, beta2 0.999, wd 0.1, aug none, 15 epochs -> best val_cos 0.9465, PEAKED ~ep11 then declined (the overfit drift we are trying to fix). ~810s/epoch on the old loader. NOTE: runs use the PILOT shard set (wds-pilot500, top-500 species, ~247k imgs) packed by pack_webdataset.py --pilot-species 500. The full-corpus shards live at wds/. --pilot-species does NOT work in --wds mode (it only filters the local-corpus path), which is why a separate pilot shard set exists.
_design:
NOT a factorial matrix -- a chain of ONE-FACTOR-AT-A-TIME comparisons from a fixed control, which is the right design for a single noisy metric on one GPU. A full 3 LR x 2 aug x 2 recipe factorial would be 12 runs (~30h) and would mostly buy interaction effects we cannot resolve at this noise level.
ORDER MATTERS: exp1 runs FIRST as a self-validating foundation (see its hypothesis). If exp1 reproduces the known pilot baseline, the shards + loader are trustworthy and everything after it is interpretable.
READ THE RESULTS AS THESE PAIRS (each differs by exactly ONE factor):
  * RECIPE : exp1 (old: wd 0.1, beta2 0.999, no warmup, no clip)
             vs exp2 (new: wd 0.2, beta2 0.95, warmup 500, clip 1.0)
  * AUG    : exp2 (aug none) vs exp3 (aug light) -- both new recipe
  * LR     : exp4/exp5/exp6 (1e-4 / 7e-5 / 5e-5), identical except --lr, all on the new recipe. Short (8 ep) because val_cos ordering is usually settled by then; the winner gets confirmed at full length afterwards.
DEFERRED interaction worth testing later (2 runs, cheap): LR x aug -- stronger aug often wants a higher LR, so the aug winner should be re-checked at the LR winner.
Runtime: 3 x 15ep (~3.5h each) + 3 x 8ep (~1.9h each) = roughly 16h total.

experiments.name: exp1_baseline_oldrecipe_ep15
experiments.hypothesis: RUNS FIRST ON PURPOSE. Full 15-epoch OLD recipe through the WebDataset path. This is the real training-viability check: it is directly comparable to the original local-corpus pilot (best val_cos 0.9465, peaked ~ep11 then declined). Gate 2 could NOT do this -- a 2-epoch run has T_max=5,154 vs the pilot's 37,875, so its cosine LR decays ~7x faster and epoch-1 numbers were never comparable. If exp1 does not land near 0.9465, STOP: something is wrong with the shards or the loader, and everything after it is built on sand.

experiments.name: exp2_newrecipe_ep15
experiments.hypothesis: CONTROL for both remaining comparisons: new recipe (warmup/grad-clip/beta2 0.95/wd 0.2), aug none, 15 epochs. Without this, phaseC is confounded -- it changes aug AND the recipe bundle vs phaseB, so a difference could not be attributed. With it: B vs B2 isolates the RECIPE BUNDLE, B2 vs C isolates AUG.

experiments.name: exp3_newrecipe_auglight_ep15
experiments.hypothesis: does light aug (RRC 0.65-1.0 + hflip) reduce the late-epoch overfit drift? Gates whether the ~56 GPU-hour multi-view caching work is worth it.

experiments.name: exp4_lr1e4_ep8
experiments.hypothesis: control: current LR at short length, to calibrate what 8 epochs looks like vs the 15-epoch baseline

experiments.name: exp5_lr7e5_ep8
experiments.hypothesis: SSOT suggests ~5-7e-5 may improve the val plateau / reduce overfit drift

experiments.name: exp6_lr5e5_ep8
experiments.hypothesis: lower end of the SSOT range; also the linear-scaling-rule value for batch 96 if 1e-4 was tuned for batch 128 (0.75x -> 7.5e-5, so 5e-5 is deliberately below)
